screens.name: Settings
screens.purpose: The app's single screen: guides the user through granting the two required system permissions, lets them customize each of the two overlay button styles (font, colors, gradient) and the shared text-length bounds, and shows a live preview of each style.
key_ui_elements: Required System Permissions card with an Overlay row and an Accessibility Service row, each showing a granted/not-granted status icon and an 'Open' button that deep-links to the matching system Settings screen
Min/Max text length fields that gate when the floating overlay buttons appear (shared by both styles)

Style 1 section: live preview, font picker (Sans Serif / Serif / Monospace / Cursive), text/background color hex fields with inline swatch + validation, gradient toggle and gradient end-color field — font size is not user-configurable; it is auto-computed from text length
Style 2 section: an identical set of controls for the second overlay button's independent style

features.name: Floating Style Overlay Triggers
features.description: A background AccessibilityService watches the actively focused editable field system-wide and shows two small floating overlay buttons — one per configured style — whenever the typed text's trimmed length falls within the user-configured min/max bounds.
acceptance_criteria: Typing in any editable field in any app shows both overlay buttons once trimmed length is within [minTextLength, maxTextLength].
The overlay buttons never appear for an empty field, even if the user configures minTextLength down to 0.
The two buttons render with visually distinct backgrounds and are independently tappable, each triggering its own style's render.
Overlay buttons hide immediately when length falls back out of bounds or focus moves to a non-editable view.
Dragging either button moves both together as a single draggable pair, and the position reacts live to settings changes without restarting the app.
features.implementation_notes: TextMonitorAccessibilityService (AccessibilityService, @AndroidEntryPoint) listens for TYPE_VIEW_TEXT_CHANGED/TYPE_VIEW_FOCUSED, tracks the current AccessibilityNodeInfo + text, and delegates the length check to a pure TextLengthEvaluator.isWithinBounds() so the boundary logic is unit-testable outside the framework. isWithinBounds() requires trimmedLength > 0 in addition to the configured [minLength, maxLength] range, guaranteeing the overlay only shows once the user has actually entered text. OverlayWindowManager stacks two ImageViews (bg_overlay_button / bg_overlay_button_secondary) inside one vertical LinearLayout container shown via a single WindowManager TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY addView/removeView; each button gets its own onClick callback (onPrimaryClicked/onSecondaryClicked) but shares one drag-listener instance so both move together. Style 1 renders with the collected TextStyleConfig; Style 2 renders with SecondaryStyleConfig.toRenderConfig(primaryConfig), which merges the secondary font/colors/gradient onto the primary config's shared paddingDp.

features.name: Styled Image Rendering
features.description: Renders the captured text into a fixed 512x512 PNG square using the current TextStyleConfig — font, text color, solid or 2-stop gradient background, and padding — with the font size auto-computed to fill the square and the text centered both horizontally and vertically. The square always has sharp corners (no border radius).
acceptance_criteria: The rendered bitmap is always exactly 512x512, regardless of text length.
Long strings wrap across multiple lines without overflowing the bitmap bounds, and font size shrinks automatically to fit.
Text is centered both horizontally and vertically within the square.
An invalid hex color string falls back to a default color instead of crashing.
features.implementation_notes: ImageRenderer.renderBitmap() binary-searches the largest text size (12px-320px) whose StaticLayout still fits the padded content area, builds the StaticLayout at that size, and draws it centered onto a fixed 512x512 Canvas-backed Bitmap with a solid or LinearGradient square background (no rounded corners — config.cornerRadiusDp is no longer read). fontSizeSp has been removed entirely from TextStyleConfig, SettingsRepository, and the Settings UI, since font size is now always auto-computed. generateStyledImageUri() writes the PNG to cacheDir/images and returns a FileProvider content URI.

features.name: Clipboard Copy & Field Clear
features.description: Tapping either overlay button copies that button's rendered image to the system clipboard as an image/png ClipData and clears the original text field, so the user can immediately paste the styled image in place of what they typed.
acceptance_criteria: After tapping either overlay button, the system clipboard holds a ClipData whose item URI resolves to image/png, rendered with the tapped button's own style.
The originating text field is cleared via ACTION_SET_TEXT immediately after the copy.
A short confirmation Toast appears telling the user to paste.
features.implementation_notes: ClipboardManagerHelper.copyImageToClipboard() uses ClipData.newUri(contentResolver, label, uri) so the MIME type is resolved from FileProvider's own getType(). TextMonitorAccessibilityService.handleStyleButtonPressed(renderConfig) is shared by both buttons' click callbacks — each passes its own resolved TextStyleConfig — then calls AccessibilityNodeInfo.performAction(ACTION_SET_TEXT, empty string) on the tracked node.

features.name: Guided Permission Setup
features.description: The Settings screen live-checks both required permissions (SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW via Settings.canDrawOverlays, the accessibility service via AccessibilityManager.getEnabledAccessibilityServiceList) on every onResume, and deep-links straight to the matching system Settings screen for whichever is missing.
acceptance_criteria: Returning to the app after granting a permission in system Settings updates that row to 'Granted' without needing to relaunch the app.
Tapping 'Open' on the overlay row launches ACTION_MANAGE_OVERLAY_PERMISSION scoped to this app's package.
Tapping 'Open' on the accessibility row launches ACTION_ACCESSIBILITY_SETTINGS.
features.implementation_notes: PermissionUtils centralizes both live checks. MainActivity re-checks both in a DefaultLifecycleObserver.onResume() and triggers Play's In-App Review flow (InAppReviewHelper) the first time both permissions transition from not-fully-granted to fully-granted — a genuine positive completion point.

features.name: Live Style Preview & Customization
features.description: Every style control across both Style 1 and Style 2 sections (font, text/background/gradient color, gradient toggle) plus the shared min/max length bounds persists to DataStore and immediately re-renders that style's live preview bitmap of sample text so the user sees the effect of a change before it's ever used on real typed text.
acceptance_criteria: Changing any Style 1 or Style 2 control updates that style's own live preview image within one recomposition, without a manual 'apply' step.
Settings for both styles persist independently across app restarts.
An invalid hex color shows an inline error state on the field instead of silently discarding the input.
features.implementation_notes: SettingsRepository wraps a single Preferences DataStore (`user_settings`) exposing TextStyleConfig (Style 1) and SecondaryStyleConfig (Style 2, under style2_* keys) as separate Flows; SettingsViewModel exposes each as its own StateFlow via stateIn(WhileSubscribed(5000)). SettingsScreen's LivePreview composable calls ImageRenderer.renderBitmap() on Dispatchers.Default inside produceState(config) and renders the result via Image(bitmap.asImageBitmap()) — called once per style, with Style 2's preview built via SecondaryStyleConfig.toRenderConfig(primaryConfig).

non_goals: No custom Input Method (IME) / system keyboard in this version — text is styled and cleared in place via AccessibilityService, not typed through a replacement keyboard.
No arbitrary number of saved style presets or a style gallery — there are exactly two fixed style slots (Style 1 / Style 2), each edited directly in Settings and each backing its own overlay button.
No in-app purchases, ads, or any billing integration — the app is entirely free with no monetization.
No handwriting font creation — only the four bundled system type families (Sans Serif, Serif, Monospace, Cursive) are offered.
No cloud backend, accounts, or sync — all settings live in local DataStore on the one device.
No app-specific one-tap share target (e.g. WhatsApp) — the styled image is placed on the system clipboard for the user to paste anywhere themselves.

steps: Call TextLengthEvaluator.isWithinBounds with lengths below, at, and above the configured min/max bounds.
Call it again with trimmedLength = 0 and minLength = 0.
test_plan.expected: Lengths strictly below minLength or strictly above maxLength return false; lengths equal to either bound or in between return true. A trimmedLength of 0 always returns false, even when minLength is 0.

test_plan.scenario: Rendered bitmap is always a fixed 512x512 square
steps: Render a short string and a long multi-sentence string with the same TextStyleConfig via ImageRenderer.renderBitmap on a connected device.
test_plan.expected: Both the short and long string bitmaps are exactly 512x512, regardless of text length.

test_plan.scenario: Invalid hex colors fall back instead of crashing
steps: Render text with a TextStyleConfig whose textColorHex and backgroundColorHex are not valid hex strings.
test_plan.expected: Rendering completes and returns a non-empty bitmap instead of throwing.

steps: Launch MainActivity via ActivityScenario so the process holds window focus.
From inside the resumed Activity, render an image and call ClipboardManagerHelper.copyImageToClipboard.
Read back ClipboardManager.primaryClip from the same focused Activity.
test_plan.expected: The primary clip's item URI matches the copied URI and its MIME type is image/png.

steps: Grant both the overlay and accessibility permissions, confirm both overlay buttons appear while typing.
Revoke one permission from system Settings, return to the app.
test_plan.expected: The revoked permission's row reverts to 'not granted' on the very next onResume, and the overlay buttons stop appearing until it's re-granted.

test_plan.scenario: Two overlay buttons with independent styles
steps: Set clearly different fonts/colors for Style 1 and Style 2 in Settings.
Type qualifying text in a monitored field and observe both floating buttons.
Drag one of the buttons and confirm both move together as a pair.
Tap the Style 1 button, paste, then repeat typing and tap the Style 2 button, paste.
test_plan.expected: Both buttons appear together and stay paired while dragging; pasting after the Style 1 tap shows an image in Style 1's look, and pasting after the Style 2 tap shows an image in Style 2's distinct look.

fields.name: font
fields.notes: maps to an Android generic Typeface family name

fields.name: backgroundColorHex
fields.notes: solid color, or gradient start color

fields.name: minTextLength
fields.notes: default 3 — overlay trigger lower bound, shared by both style buttons

fields.name: maxTextLength
fields.notes: default 280 — overlay trigger upper bound, shared by both style buttons

fields.name: font
fields.notes: default SERIF, independent of the primary style's font

fields.name: backgroundColorHex
fields.notes: default #F5E9DA — solid color, or gradient start color

data_model.notes: Backs the second overlay button. Only visual fields — paddingDp, minTextLength, and maxTextLength are borrowed from TextStyleConfig via SecondaryStyleConfig.toRenderConfig(base) when rendering.

libraries.purpose: Android Kotlin extensions and compatibility helpers
Local key-value storage for the one active TextStyleConfig
Coroutines for DataStore flows and the accessibility service's settings collector
Dependency injection into the Application, Activity, and AccessibilityService
Play In-App Review prompt after first successful permission setup

positioning: Type anywhere — any app, any field — and turn what you typed into a beautifully styled image with one tap on a small floating button, ready to paste right back in.

design_system.typography: Google Fonts 'Fraunces' (serif, expressive) for in-app headings/branding, Material 3 default type scale (Roboto Flex) for all other UI chrome and body text — never used for the rendered style output itself, which always uses the user's selected style font.
design_system.theme_notes: Dark mode follows the system default: light theme uses background #F7F5FF / surface #FFFFFF / on-background #1C1B1F; dark theme uses background #16151F / surface #201F2C / on-background #E7E1FF.

store_listing.title: InkSend: Style Any Text
store_listing.icon_prompt: Create a 1024x1024 Android app icon for InkSend, a text-styling utility app. Rounded-square adaptive icon style, indigo background (#5B47E0), a simple white fountain-pen nib icon with a short flowing ink stroke. Flat vector design, high contrast, no text, no brand logos, no photorealistic elements.
store_listing.long_description:
InkSend turns anything you type, in any app, into a beautifully styled image — your choice of font, text color, and background — ready to paste back in with one tap.

Just start typing in any text field. Once your message is long enough, two small floating buttons appear, one for each of your two saved styles. Tap either one, and InkSend renders your exact words as a styled image in that look, copies it to your clipboard, and clears the field — so a long-press and Paste (or your keyboard's clipboard suggestion) drops the image right back in.

Customize both styles from one simple settings screen: font, text color, background color or gradient, and exactly which text lengths should trigger the buttons — with a live preview of each style as you go. Font size always auto-fits your text, so there's nothing to fiddle with.

Everything happens on your device. No account, no ads, no subscription — InkSend is completely free.
store_listing.short_description: Style any text you type and paste it back in as an image — free, no ads, no account.

project_context: This spec describes an independent, alternative Android app you are building from scratch to compete with an existing incumbent app on Google Play — not a modification, clone, or reskin of the incumbent's own code, assets, or branding. Use the incumbent only as a market reference (via the report data below), and design working_name/package_id/store_listing/design_system so the result is clearly its own product.
build_instructions:
chmod +x ./gradlew
./gradlew clean
./gradlew testDebugUnitTest
./gradlew connectedDebugAndroidTest
keytool -genkeypair -v -keystore inksend-upload.jks -storetype JKS -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 -alias upload -dname "CN=InkSend Upload,O=AppyFYI,C=US" -storepass changeit -keypass changeit
RELEASE_STORE_FILE="$PWD/inksend-upload.jks" RELEASE_STORE_PASSWORD="changeit" RELEASE_KEY_ALIAS="upload" RELEASE_KEY_PASSWORD="changeit" ./gradlew bundleRelease
